type.description: Read config.yml 'prefix' option for info.
The reason this doesn't support multiple words is that it'll minimize the amount of inputs players can choose for all the chat inputs.
User-defined display names for Minecraft worlds.
Used for displaying no limit. Currently only used for invite codes.
Used for boolean placeholder modifier.
Translated text used when a true value is shown to a player.
Translated text used when a false value is shown to a player.
Used in places were the data is no longer available. For example, a kingdom that sent a mail was disbanded.
Used where a defined message language entry in a config isn't set in the language file.
Used for absence of a value.
Used as a generic title for GUI errors when clicking on items.
Used when the [item] feature is used in chat without having any item in you target slot.
Used for siege cannon ammo names.
Used for words when they're configured outside of language files.

Used for time-based placeholders. The default time related placeholders like %kingdoms_shield_time% are shown as random numbers if you use it just like that, you'd have to use the timer modifier: %kingdoms_time_shield_time%
It uses Java's default date formatter syntax which can be found here: https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/time/format/DateTimeFormatter.html#patterns
Used for /k map and /k claim line
Reusable message variables referenced as {$name}.
Messages mostly used for /k map
The following values are used when no custom message is set for certain actions.
Used for commands that support numbers which are relative to something else.
Channel display name.
Compact channel name.
